note: The citing work references Stephenson et al. 2003a to justify choosing genetic programming for compiler problems ('due to its high level of flexibility at generating functions for compiler problems that are poorly understood'), and separately describes Stephenson et al. 2003b's results (9% improvement on hyperblock formation) to support the claim that genetic programming has potential for compiler heuristics — specific findings travel into the argument.
title: Adaptive Source-Level Data Assignment to Dual Memory Banks
